subject: Dedicated commit: validation methodology, penalty calibration, and billing staircase
messages:

Cc: ops@finserve.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit — validation expectations and billing questions

Thanks Mina — quick follow up from our infra team after the demo. We like the Dedicated model but need clarity on three things before procurement:

1) How does Redwood measure tokens/sec and requests/sec for acceptance testing? Do you run synthetic load or replay production logs?
2) What are the latency targets tied to the commit (p50/p95)? If you miss them, how do penalty credits work?
3) How do reserved commit bands map to billing — is there a staircase for discounts or a linear rate?

Can you share a short acceptance test plan and any sample output from a baseline run?

--
Elena Petrova
Head of Cloud Platforms, FinServe
elena@finserve.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated commit — validation expectations and billing questions

Thanks Elena — great questions. I put together an overview (high level) and attached our test harness + a recent baseline CSV from a QA run. Key points below; Rishi and Marissa are cc'ed for SRE specifics and commercial framing.

Summary (short):
- Measurement approach: we prefer a two-stage validation: 1) synthetic controlled load (our harness) to validate tokens/sec and request/sec deterministically; 2) optional production replay if you want your traffic shape run. The harness supports warm-cache and cold-cache modes.
- Throughput metrics: tokens/sec measured as aggregated generated tokens over the test window; requests/sec measured as completed inference calls/second. We report p50/p90/p95 latencies per route and tokens/sec broken down by sequence-length bucket.
- Latency targets and credits: default target is p95 <= 350ms for standard gen routes (sequence <= 256). If we miss the committed p95 in two consecutive measurement windows we offer service credits proportionate to the measured miss (formula in SOW).
- Billing/discounts: reserved commit bands (three tiers) map to unit-rate discounts in a staircase: larger commits reduce per-token price in defined bands; there is also a burn-rate carve-out for burst capacity. Commercial details are proposed by Marissa.

Attachments: dedicated_commit_test_harness_v1.zip (test harness + README), baseline-benchmark-20270430.csv (sample run), SOW_FinServe_Dedicated_2027-05.pdf (draft with proposed credit formula).

If useful, propose a 2-hour validation window next week where we run the harness and produce an acceptance report you can sign off on.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Engineer — Dedicated Solutions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. To put commercial framing on Mina's notes:
- Commit bands: Starter (50M tokens/mo), Scale (200M tokens/mo), Enterprise (1B+ tokens/mo). Each band has a stepped per-token price; moving between bands resets to the higher discount once the monthly commit threshold is reached. We can offer an early-signing discount (one-time) for a 12-month commit.
- Penalty calibration: credits are capped at a percentage of the monthly invoice to avoid over-indexing. The SOW includes examples.
- GPU sizing: we propose a 2x safety buffer for the first 90 days (based on your peak shape) then move to traffic-based autoscaling rules.

If you have internal procurement constraints (e.g., fixed PO cycles or required invoice terms), tell me and I'll align the proposal.

Best,
Marissa

Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Elena — a few technical clarifications from the acceptance-testing side:

1) Warm vs. cold cache: our harness can run a warm-cache profile (preload KV cache + prefix caching) which reflects steady-state throughput. Cold-cache gives a worst-case baseline for cache miss penalty. We always report both if you ask.
2) Measurement window: standard is a rolling 10-minute window for throughput and a 30-minute run for durability checks. For final acceptance we do three replicates separated by 15 minutes; acceptance passes if two of three replicates meet the committed metrics.
3) Network jitter and region: tests should run from your on-prem or VPC egress to match production network RTTs; if you run tests from our hosted region we annotate measured network RTT and exclude network-induced latency from credits if the RTT exceeds an agreed threshold.
4) Bench harness determinism: seeds and input traces are recorded in the harness output. We provide full logs and token-level timestamps for audit.

Practical ask: please share a representative 48-hour traffic sample (anonymized) or pick one of our standard shapes (chat-heavy vs single-turn generation) so we can size the GPU pool and pick the most appropriate measurement buckets.

-Rishi
Senior SRE, Dedicated Platforms

- Ops will provide a 48-hour anonymized trace by end of day Monday. We'll ask to run the validation from our VPC egress to replicate network conditions.
- On cost: we are leaning toward the Scale band but would like the 12-month early-signing discount, and to understand how month-to-month overages are billed versus committed tokens (units or prorated?).

Also, please confirm whether the initial GPU buffer incurs additional monthly charge or is included in the committed price for the ramp period.

—Elena

Elena — quick answers and next steps:

- SOW clause: see section 4.2 (page 5) in the attached SOW_FinServe_Dedicated_2027-05.pdf — it lists the credit formula and the monthly cap (10% of the monthly invoice) with worked examples. I'll pull the exact excerpt into a follow-up email for procurement.
- GPU buffer: the 2x safety buffer is operational guidance; for commercial clarity we can include the buffer in the committed bill for the first 90 days at the agreed commit rate (no extra charge) provided you sign the 12-month commit. After 90 days we move to actual-utilization autoscaling for billing adjustments.
- Overages: billed at the next band rate on a prorated basis for the settlement period; overage math is in section 2.3 of the SOW.

Next steps: 1) we'll accept your offer to provide the anonymized trace; 2) Rishi will schedule the harness run once we have the trace and VPC egress details; 3) Marissa will update the commercial terms and send a clean SOW + one-page summary for procurement.

I'll follow up Monday with an excerpt for procurement and a proposed time window for the validation run.

Thanks,
Mina
